goal: Keep the armed per-prompt recall query process and index warm (#153)
asset: The existing offline recall search and precision floor
scope: Node warm hook client and detached startup
Index cache invalidation and idle cleanup
Existing root selection and offline hook behavior
outOfScope: Index rebuilds or embedding network calls in the query process

record.question: How should decisions and requirements constrain implementation?

options.strongest_objection: Adds a manifest and lock that must be revised when requirements change
The existing compiler accepts mutating graphs with no spec or decisions
Would require new models and checker support for every implementation language

record.rationale: Use an authenticated loopback query process and a portable Node hook client while preserving existing offline precision-floored recall. Keep source/index caches in memory with file-stat invalidation, bound requests and idle lifetime, and detach standard handles at startup.
evidence: Issue #153 measured 2.6 second armed prompts from repeated Python/index cold starts. Read prompt-recall.sh, lib.sh project jurisdiction, recall.for_prompt and ensure_index.

costs.cost: Two tracked artifacts and requirement-specific check maintenance
evidence: Design scope; no elapsed implementation time estimate claimed

costs.cost: No new runtime checks; unmet requirements can remain invisible
evidence: Mutating graph without spec compiled with exit 0

costs.cost: Per-language proof and conformance work with unmeasured maintenance cost
evidence: Existing proof integrations have different semantics; no universal adapter exists in this repository

requirements.statement: An armed warm prompt reuses Python and index state, honors root containment and the precision floor, detects replaced index files, authenticates requests and responses, bounds input/output and idle lifetime, and inherits no hook pipes; failures retain bounded cold fallback.
requirements.counterexample: A second prompt starts Python again, serves replaced index content, accepts an unauthenticated request, or waits forever on a detached child holding hook stdout.

checks.scope: Execute daemon protocol, warm hook reuse, cache invalidation, limits and idle cleanup
assumptions: Local same-user processes and the existing recall search are trusted; tests exercise actual loopback requests and hook scripts.

challenges.claim: A stale port may belong to a different local process
challenges.resolution: Requests and responses use nonce-bound HMAC authentication; the bearer secret is never transmitted.
